title: Context Managers Basics & the with statement

slides.title: Understanding Context Managers & the `with` statement
slides.prompt: Context managers simplify resource management by ensuring setup and cleanup code execution around a block of statements. The `with` statement handles resource acquisition and release automatically, even if exceptions occur.
slides.codeSnippet:
# Resource handling without `with` vs with `with`
# Manual approach
f = open('example.txt', 'w')
try:
    f.write('Hello World')
finally:
    f.close()

# Modern Pythonic approach
with open('example.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write('Hello World')

slides.title: The `with` Keyword Syntax
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword used to wrap execution of a block with methods defined by a context manager.

slides.title: Primary Benefit of Context Managers
slides.prompt: What is the primary advantage of using a context manager when working with external resources like files or database connections?
options: Guaranteed cleanup/closure of resources regardless of errors
Faster execution time due to C-level optimizations
Automatic conversion of byte streams to strings
slides.correctAnswer: Guaranteed cleanup/closure of resources regardless of errors

slides.title: Multiple Context Managers
slides.prompt: How can you manage multiple resources simultaneously using the `with` statement in modern Python?
options: By separating multiple context manager calls with commas inside a single `with` statement or using parentheses
By nesting `with` statements inside separate functions only
By joining context managers using the `and` logical operator
Context managers can only handle one resource at a time
slides.correctAnswer: By separating multiple context manager calls with commas inside a single `with` statement or using parentheses

slides.title: Context Manager Reusability
slides.prompt: What happens if a built-in file context manager object is reused across multiple `with` statements?
options: It raises a ValueError or I/O error because closed file streams cannot be re-opened directly
It automatically resets the file cursor back to index 0
It appends new data to the existing file pointer
It creates a duplicate copy of the file on disk
slides.correctAnswer: It raises a ValueError or I/O error because closed file streams cannot be re-opened directly
